blocks.text: `std.hash` offers SHA-256/384/512, SHA-3, SHAKE, HMAC, HKDF and PBKDF2; the code is portable Greengold and needs no libc. Byte data goes in as `[]u8` (a `List[u8]`, an array or `text.as_bytes()`). `std.encoding` turns byte arrays into hexadecimal or base64 text.

**Never compare** digests or MACs **with `==`**: a measurable time difference leaks information. Use `crypto.constant_time_eq`. `std.crypto` also offers ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-GCM, X25519, Ed25519 and the self-wiping `SecretBytes`.

blocks.prompt: Compute the SHA-256 digests of `"abc"` and `"abd"`, compare them with `crypto.constant_time_eq` and print the result.
blocks.hint: The digests are `[32]u8` arrays; turn them into slices with `a[..]`.

blocks.q: Why use `constant_time_eq` instead of `==` to compare two digests?
options: Because a timing difference can leak information
blocks.why: A constant-time comparison does not stop at the first differing byte.
